Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: The plan provides a comprehensive district-wide inventory including building age, size, classroom counts, and detailed site diagrams for all schools (Sections 4, pages 18-86). It includes detailed condition assessments covering major systems and identifies both immediate and long-term needs, linking these to modernization eligibility and capital planning (Sections 4, pages 18-86).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: The plan includes detailed enrollment projections over a 6-year horizon with methodology explained (Section 3, pages 12-16). It provides capacity utilization data by site and classroom, discusses under- and over-utilization, and connects these analyses to facility actions such as portable replacement and new construction (Sections 3 and 7).

Educational Alignment.justification: The plan references educational goals and programs in broad terms and mentions some program spaces (e.g., cafeterias, multi-use rooms) but lacks detailed educational specifications or explicit connections between facility projects and instructional needs (Executive Summary and Section 4).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: There is no mention or analysis of outdoor spaces, greening, shade, or outdoor learning in the plan. Site maps show outdoor spaces only as playgrounds or parking without discussion of green space or environmental benefits (Sections 4 and 5).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: The plan does not mention climate risks or climate readiness/resilience strategies. Emergency preparedness is not linked to climate change impacts (entire document).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: There is no mention of energy efficiency, electrification, decarbonization, or energy resilience strategies. No data on energy use or reference to state requirements such as Title 24 or Zero Net Energy goals (entire document).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: The plan presents a detailed financial strategy including itemized cost estimates, funding sources (state programs, local bonds, developer fees), and a clear prioritization framework based on community input and project urgency (Sections 6 and 7, pages 93-104). It includes phasing plans and discusses long-term financial sustainability.
